# Spiritual Translation

---

**¶1:**

[GAP-1] upon [GAP-2] from [GAP-3] thus [GAP-4]

*Almost nothing survives in the natural text here. The connecting words "upon… from… thus" suggest a foundational statement of spiritual causation — one reality proceeding from another according to divine order. The spiritual content of the four gaps cannot be determined from the residue alone.*

---

**¶2:**

[GAP-5] the wholeness of these states [GAP-6] that they shall [GAP-7] seven complete forms of the spiritual will [GAP-8] Again, he too, this very [GAP-9: spiritual principle or agent] — in the state when [GAP-10] of Divine Wisdom [GAP-11] the entire mind in its fullness [GAP-12] is opened to interior perception [GAP-13] is restored to Divine Wisdom [GAP-14] completely, according to the essential manner in which he subsists [GAP-15] proceeding from [GAP-16] these remaining three degrees [GAP-17]

---

## Notes on key correspondences:

- **"seven people"** → *seven complete forms of the spiritual will*: Seven denotes a full series from first to last; "people" as living agents correspond to volitional affections or discrete states of the regenerating life.
- **"the Light"** (appearing twice) → *Divine Wisdom*: Light in correspondence is always truth proceeding from the Divine — here, the origin and the destination of restoration.
- **"the universe"** → *the entire mind in its fullness*: The cosmos in the ancient teaching substrate corresponds to the Grand Human or, more immediately, to the whole organic structure of the regenerating mind.
- **"is revealed"** → *is opened to interior perception*: Revelation is not mere disclosure but the actual opening of an interior degree to conscious spiritual sight.
- **"take to the Light"** → *restored to Divine Wisdom*: The movement toward Light is the reordering of what had fallen into falsity back into the sphere of truth from the Divine.
- **"these other three"** → *these remaining three degrees*: Three signifies what is complete as to degrees — likely the three discrete degrees of the mind (celestial, spiritual, natural), or three essential divine qualities yet to be unified with the seven states above.

*The passage, despite its extreme fragmentation, preserves the outline of a teaching about the full restoration of all states of the spiritual will (seven) to Divine Wisdom, accomplished through a specific spiritual agency, with three further degrees or principles completing the process.*

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: [He shall gather a]ll of them [and refine them so] that they shall [be purified and come forth as] seven people [who shall serve in the Light] Again, he too, this per[son, at] the time when [the mystery] of the Light [comes upon] the universe [and it] is revealed [and he shall] take to the Light [and purify them utt]erly, the way that he exists [and comes forth] from [among] these other three [powers]

fills.explanation: The preposition "upon" followed by "from" suggests an agent acting upon recipients from a divine source — "upon them" is a standard Kephalaia construction for divine action directed at persons.
The spiritual reading indicates divine causation — "from the Father" is the standard Manichaean expression for the ultimate divine source from which agents and powers proceed.
"Thus he came" naturally completes the causal chain of being sent upon them from the Father — the result of the divine sending is the agent's arrival.

The spiritual reading maps "all of them" to "the wholeness of these states" being restored; "gather" is the quintessential Manichaean verb for the restoration of scattered light, and the fill's terminal "a" joins with "ll" to form "all."
The gap bridges the gathering of "all of them" to the purpose clause "that they shall"; refining/purifying is the central Manichaean process by which scattered elements are restored to ordered forms.

fills.fill: be purified and come forth as
fills.explanation: The gap requires a verb between "shall" and "seven people"; the spiritual reading identifies these as "seven complete forms of the spiritual will," requiring both purification and manifestation — "come forth as" is standard Kephalaia language for ordered emanation.

fills.fill: who shall serve in the Light
fills.explanation: The gap concludes the description of the seven people before transitioning to a new agent; the spiritual reading identifies them as complete forms of the will, whose purpose is service within Divine Wisdom — "serve in the Light" is a natural Kephalaia predicate for ordered agents.

The fill completes "person" and bridges to the temporal clause "the time when"; the spiritual reading identifies this as a specific spiritual agent, and "at" provides the natural preposition connecting the agent to the temporal clause.

"The mystery of the Light" is a core Kephalaia expression, and the later verb "is revealed" perfectly completes it — mysteries being revealed is the quintessential structure of Manichaean teaching, corresponding to Divine Wisdom opening interior perception.

The gap connects "of the Light" to "the universe"; the spiritual reading maps this to Divine Wisdom acting upon the entire mind — "comes upon" expresses the descent of the Light's mystery upon the cosmos, a standard Manichaean formulation for divine action on the world.

The gap bridges "the universe" to "is revealed"; the spiritual reading indicates the universe/mind being opened to perception — "and it" provides the necessary conjunction and pronoun referring back to the mystery or the universe.

The gap connects "is revealed" to "take to the Light"; the spiritual reading indicates an act of restoration to Divine Wisdom — "he" refers back to the specific person/agent introduced earlier, and "shall" maintains the future prophetic tense of the passage.

The fill bridges "take to the Light" to "utterly"; the spiritual reading indicates complete restoration — purification is the essential Manichaean process of restoration, and "utt" joins with "erly" to form "utterly," expressing the completeness of the work.

The gap bridges "the way that he exists" to "from these other three"; the spiritual reading indicates the agent's mode of subsistence as proceeding from the three degrees — "comes forth" is the standard Kephalaia verb for emanation/proceeding from a source.

"From among" is a standard Kephalaia prepositional phrase indicating origin within a group; the spiritual reading's "proceeding from these remaining three degrees" implies the agent's existence originates from within the three.

The spiritual reading identifies "these other three" as "three degrees" — in the Kephalaia's natural-plane vocabulary, discrete degrees of divine operation correspond to "powers," the standard Manichaean term for ordered divine agents/forces.
